summary: Susan Neiman is a philosopher who studied at Harvard (Ph.D. ~1977–1986) and the Free University of Berlin. She held professorships at Yale (1989–1996) and Tel Aviv University (1996–2000), and served as Director of the Einstein Forum (2000–2026).
Susan Niditch is a religious studies scholar who spent her career at Amherst College, serving in the religion department from ~1978 to 2020.

Susan Whitfield is a scholar of Central Asian, Chinese, and historical studies who earned her PhD at SOAS (1995). She directed the International Dunhuang Project at the British Library (1993–2017) and became Professor in Silk Road Studies at the Sainsbury Institute.

Susanne Hoeber Rudolph (1930–2015) was a political scientist and Indologist who studied at Sarah Lawrence, Harvard (MA, PhD), and Radcliffe (PhD). She taught at Harvard (~1955–1963) and became a professor at the University of Chicago in 1964.

Susanne Mrozik is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who earned an M.T.S. at Harvard, studying with Charles Hallisey, Diana L. Eck, Stephanie W. Jamison, and Margaret R. Miles. She held posts at Western Michigan University and Mount Holyoke College.

Sushanta Sen is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Indology who studied at Visva-Bharati University. He served as a lecturer at Visva-Bharati (1986) and as Lecturer in Indian Religions in theology at the University of Birmingham.

Sushil Kumar De (1890–1968) was an Indologist educated at Presidency College, Calcutta University, and SOAS (D.Litt.). He taught at Calcutta, was Professor of Sanskrit at Dhaka (~1923–1947), and led the Bengali department at Jadavpur University (~1956–1961).

Susumu Kajiura is a scholar of Sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He served as an assistant at Kyoto University in 1999 and headed humanities research at the Gangoji Institute for Research on Cultural Property (attested 2001).

Susumu Otake is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at the University of Tsukuba (~1993–2002) under Makio Takemura. He has held teaching posts at Kyoto University, Hanazono University, and Bukkyo University.

Susumu Shimazono is a scholar of religious studies and Japanology who studied at the University of Tokyo. He taught at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies and served as Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Tokyo (1995–2013).

Susumu Yamaguchi (1895–1976) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology who studied at Otani and Kyoto Universities, Sylvain Lévi, and Louis de La Vallée Poussin. He served as a professor at Otani University (1934–1964).

Suwanda H. J. Sugunasiri is a Buddhist studies scholar educated at the University of London, University of Pennsylvania, and University of Toronto (PhD). He founded and served as president of Nalanda College of Buddhist Studies and taught at Ontario Tech University.

Suzanne Karpelès (1890–1968) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the EPHE under Sylvain Lévi, Alfred Foucher, and Louis Finot. She served at EFEO (1922–1941) and directed Cambodia's National Library and Buddhist Institute.

Suzanne Newcombe is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who earned her doctorate at the University of Cambridge. She has held posts at Cambridge, LSE, Inform, and the Open University, where she is a senior lecturer.

Sven Hedin (1865–1952) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He completed his studies at the universities of Stockholm, Uppsala, Berlin, and Halle-Wittenberg between 1886 and 1892.
Sven Wittemann is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts degree at the International Buddhist College under the supervision of Kapila Abhayawansa (attested 2014).

Swami Dayananda Saraswati (1930–2015) was a teacher of Advaita philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at Bangalore Sanskrit College and trained with Chinmayananda Saraswati, Swami Tapovan Maharaj, Swami Pranavananda, and Swami Tarananda Giri.

Swami Lakshman Joo (1907–1991) was a scholar and master of Shaiva philosophy, Indology, and religious studies who studied under Maheshwar Nath Razdan (1926–1933). In 1991, he founded the Universal Shaiva Fellowship.

Swami Maheshanandagiri Maharaj was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who served as Mahamandaleshvar Pontiff of Dakshinamurti Peetha (attested 1980). He founded the Mahesh Research Institute and Advaita Grantha Ratna Manjusha.
Swami Satyananda Puri (1902–1942) was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Indology who studied at the University of Calcutta (~1920–1926) and later held a post there.
